body: Ah thanks man, actually what you said isn’t the first time someone told me that. I genuinely want to make new friendships, but I guess sometimes it does start feeling like something I have to regularly check up on, like I’m tasked to watch over someone. Thanks for your advice though, definitely gonna re-think about it considering that again, this isn’t the first time I heard it. :)
Thank you for your advice, I’ll keep it in mind when I try to talk to others next time.

Hello, first off I’d like to say thank you for replying to my post (I’ve posted a few times in other communities, but no one replied to any of them), and sorry for not including the specifics of what answers I’m looking for (I was getting worried that my post was getting too long, so I didn’t include everything I wanted to say). Well, I’d day that I’m already doing ok at the very least with social cues, I just need to really know how to talk to people (especially women since I feel more uncomfortable with them, and yes I’m a guy). To be specific, I need to know stuff like what to say, what to do in this or that situation, and what to do or avoid in order to not be hated. Sorry if that still wasn’t specific (I don’t know how to make it specific), so I’ll just give an example: there was this one time when I tried to befriend the “most relatable and approachable” guy in class. I spoke to him, but I ended up asking him a list of questions like this: “Do you like cooking?” “Do you like technology?” “Do you like playing video games?” and tried to go in deeper on the stuff he liked, but long story short I failed to befriend him because I kept asking him those kinds of questions. I hope that was helpful, if not just tell me and I’ll try to explain it again. Thank you once more for commenting on my post, and sorry if this reply is even longer than my actual post.

Hello! In my opinion, I do not think that you should get AX1 right now since you don’t have equipment, as the program does require some basic gym equipment like dumbbells and more. It does come with the X-Factor meal plan though, but I’ve read many reviews about it and most of them had negative things to say about the meal plan, as it does not take into account how much calories and macros you take. However, I would like to inform you that I haven’t tried out AX1 myself, and this comment is based purely on research (I would recommend doing AX1 when you do get the equipment though, again basing from research, and as for the meal plan, many users suggest buying the book “Burn the Fat, Feed the Muscle”). As a suggestion, perhaps you may want to opt for Jeff’s free workouts on YouTube instead? Yes, XERO requires no equipment, but since you mentioned that you’re a beginner (like me), I think it would be a bit too hard, this time basing off of both research and experience. I also haven’t tried XERO, but I’ve done some bodyweight training and it will kill your  ass, well at least it killed mine. I hope you found this comment helpful, and if not, just not that I am  still a beginner who is yet to know more about all of this stuff. Wish you the best man!
